title: "Week 12 — Visualization for ML/NLP"
---

> Visualizing machine learning and natural language processing outputs for interpretability and insight.


## 📖 Background & Motivation

Modern machine learning and NLP models generate complex outputs — from feature importances and prediction probabilities to topic clusters and embeddings. Visualization provides the bridge between model mechanics and human understanding. This week focuses on how to visualize model performance, interpret model decisions, and explore textual data patterns.

---

## 🔎 Learning Objectives

- Plot feature importance for classification and regression models.
- Visualize model performance with confusion matrices and ROC curves.
- Use embeddings and clustering visualizations to interpret NLP models.
- Generate word clouds and topic cluster plots using BERTopic.
- Understand visualization's role in the ML workflow for interpretability and trust.

---

## 💻 Starter Notebook Snippets

### Feature Importance Plot

::: {#ff24ae86 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True, as_frame=True)
model = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42).fit(X, y)
importances = pd.Series(model.feature_importances_, index=X.columns).sort_values()

importances.plot(kind='barh', color='#4e79a7')
plt.title('Feature Importance — Random Forest')
plt.xlabel('Importance Score')
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](week_12_viz_ml_nlp_files/figure-html/cell-2-output-1.png){width=667 height=449}
:::
:::


### Confusion Matrix and ROC Curve

::: {#e0bbe4e4 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from sklearn.metrics import ConfusionMatrixDisplay, RocCurveDisplay, classification_report
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

# The full confusion matrix works for all three iris classes.
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred = model.predict(X_test)

ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_estimator(model, X_test, y_test)
plt.title('Confusion Matrix (3 classes)')
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](week_12_viz_ml_nlp_files/figure-html/cell-3-output-1.png){width=509 height=449}
:::
:::


A ROC curve is defined for a **binary** classifier, so we reduce iris to two classes
(versicolor vs. virginica) to illustrate it:

::: {#3447604b .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# Binary subset for a ROC curve
mask = y.isin([1, 2])
Xb, yb = X[mask], (y[mask] == 2).astype(int)   # 1 = virginica, 0 = versicolor

Xb_tr, Xb_te, yb_tr, yb_te = train_test_split(Xb, yb, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)
binary_model = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42).fit(Xb_tr, yb_tr)

RocCurveDisplay.from_estimator(binary_model, Xb_te, yb_te)
plt.title('ROC Curve (versicolor vs. virginica)')
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](week_12_viz_ml_nlp_files/figure-html/cell-4-output-1.png){width=445 height=449}
:::
:::


### Word Cloud and Topic Clusters

```python
from wordcloud import WordCloud
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

text = ' '.join(['great movie', 'terrible film', 'excellent acting', 'boring story'])
wc = WordCloud(width=600, height=300, background_color='white').generate(text)
plt.imshow(wc, interpolation='bilinear')
plt.axis('off')
plt.title('Example Word Cloud')
plt.show()
```

```python
from bertopic import BERTopic
from sklearn.datasets import fetch_20newsgroups

newsgroups = fetch_20newsgroups(subset='all')
docs = newsgroups.data[:200]

model = BERTopic(verbose=True)
topics, probs = model.fit_transform(docs)
model.visualize_topics()
```
